body:
PR #1994 for BUG-1294 — 64 flags swept, and there is a tradeoff inherent to the fix that I want a reviewer to weigh rather than discover

Open on bug-1294. Both lanes are now in: #1993 and #1994. No verdict from me on either; I wrote both prompts.

THE SWEEP IS GENUINE. `allow_hyphen_values` on 64 prose-taking flags, not the two that were reported. The list covers add/edit titles and descriptions, doc add, comment content, report bug/idea, merge-hold and pr hold reasons, session titles, review summaries, db sync messages, queue rework reasons, questions rationale and notes, findings notes, punt reasons and leans, advisor handoff focus, agent prompts, defer --until, brief notes. That is your "fix the class, not the instance".

The exclusions are the part I would check: --tags, ids, paths, SHAs, date filters, enum-like short tokens such as --category and --classification, short identifiers such as --name, and positionals. Those look right to me — a hyphen-leading value is not a plausible tag or enum member — but it is a judgement call made 64 times and it is where a wrong call would hide.

THE GUARD HOLDS, and I read the test rather than taking the claim:

  Cli::try_parse_from(["aida", "add", "--titel", "probe"]) -> unwrap_err()

`allow_hyphen_values` widens only what a flag's OWN value may look like; clap still matches `--foo` tokens against declared names, so a genuine typo still errors. Tested for both add and edit.

THE TRADEOFF, which is inherent to the fix rather than a defect in it, and which nobody has named yet. After this change:

  aida add --title --force

parses `--force` as the VALUE of --title and creates a spec titled "--force", where today it errors. That is the intended behaviour — it is the same mechanism that lets us file a bug titled "--format json returns human text" — but it means a user who forgets a value now gets a wrongly-titled spec instead of a parse error. The lane tested that case and treated it as correct, which I think it is, but it is a real behaviour change at 64 sites and it deserves a deliberate yes rather than being inherited from the mechanism.

If you want it narrowed, the obvious lever is to apply allow_hyphen_values only where a hyphen-leading value is actually plausible — titles, descriptions, reasons, notes — and leave it off for the flags where a missing value is the likelier mistake. That would be a smaller sweep and a defensible one.

Reported, not re-run by me: 5101 tests pass, fmt clean, and `aida add --help` / `aida edit --help` spot-checked for trace-marker leakage with none found — which matters more than usual here, since this PR edits clap definitions where a `///` comment IS help output.

One process note: this lane ran `cargo fmt --all` once to fix drift from the mechanical edits, then `--check` clean. That is the right order and worth noting only because the standing rule is "never bare cargo fmt" — the rule exists so a dirty tree is not masked before a check, and running it deliberately then verifying is not the failure the rule guards against.
